chapter: Pictures, Oliver, Armstrong and Fat Pichon
title: Friendship with Fats Pichon
summary: Arthur talks about boyhood friend Fats Pichon, his son and his health, and how marriage drew them apart.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues

blocks.x: Okay. All right. And you know, I was speaking to Fat's son.
Fat Pechon's son? Yeah. I didn't know he had a son.

Oh, he's got a boy. If you see his boy, you'll sway him. Really? Yeah, a fine boy. I didn't know that. Built just about like you. I was speaking to him in the hardware store Monday. And I asked him about his daddy's cell. I spoke to him Sunday long distance. He said he's not any better. He said he's not any better. That's the boy I raised up with me. We come up with little kids together. Fat nine.
I don't guess Fat's will ever get his sight back. It's tough. Yeah.
Next time he comes in town, you ought to interview Fat's. Yeah, we've never interviewed him.
We've talked a lot. He knows a lot. Oh, yeah, yeah.

You see, what kept him up with them, he kept up with the music, you see. And when Fat's got married, he and I were buddies like that. You could tell the way we got together. We were old time buddies. His mother partly raised me. See, my mother died when I was 12. His mother partly raised me. Now Fat's and I were together, but when he got married, I was still single. He got married before me. And that made a difference in him and I because every time we'd go out, his wife could blame me for it. Yeah. So then I pulled away from him, but he continued with the music life. And he contacted more of the musicians than I did, you see, because I was in the music life. And then we would be out, but very seldom. Whenever he would come out and meet me, we'd go out, but I wouldn't go to the house anymore and take him out because his wife would always claim that I didn't have no wife and I'd keep him out all night. You see, no, I wouldn't call him. So that just tore us two apart. But every time he'd come in, he'd send me his picture or he'd write a letter. I showed you pictures that he had here. Did I show you his picture here? No, I haven't saw it. Let's see, I have a picture of it where he moved me. I got some from Henry.
